descriptor.name: spaces
descriptor.label: Spaces
descriptor.description: Run whole machines on a Leo hub — install the hypervisor, create Windows and Linux guests, and hand one a GPU.
descriptor.details: Turns a Leo hub or compute machine into a hypervisor, then runs guests on it. The Host setup tab reports what the box is — distribution, CPU, IOMMU, graphics devices, whether anything can be isolated for a guest — and derives the remaining steps fresh on every load, so a step that became true disappears. Guests are KVM/QEMU domains managed through libvirt: define one, start it, snapshot it, assign it a GPU exclusively. Windows guests get UEFI firmware, a software TPM and the virtio driver ISO without being asked, because all three are what a Windows install needs and the failures when they are missing look like broken storage. Everything privileged goes through one root-owned wrapper with a closed verb set; without it this package still reports and plans, and hands over the exact commands.
descriptor.setup_hint: Install it on the box you want to virtualise on and leave the host field blank — `leo packages install descriptor.json --on <box> --enabled` does the whole thing, including placing this package's root-owned wrapper and the one sudoers rule for its ten verbs (that is the privileged_helper block below, and the install asks before it does it). Then one command as an admin on that box: `leo mcp add spaces /var/lib/leo/apps/spaces/src/target/release/leo-spaces mcp` — an app package never gets its own MCP server, so the tools need this. To drive a remote host instead, mint it a token for its own settings first (leo packages token mint spaces --scope settings:read) and pass it as --token.
use_cases: Turn the work hub into a hypervisor without a console
Run Windows-only CAD and simulation software on Linux metal
Give one guest the GPU outright, and see why another cannot have it
Snapshot a machine before letting an agent loose on it

action.message: Cuts the power without telling the guest. Unsaved work is lost, and a guest writing to disk can be left with a damaged filesystem. Use Shut down unless it has stopped responding.

privileged_helper.purpose: turn this box into a hypervisor: the packages, libvirt, the guest network and storage, the IOMMU kernel parameters, and binding a PCI device to vfio-pci so a guest can own it

verbs.what: print the wrapper's version — what the package probes to tell a usable grant from a file nothing can run
install qemu, libvirt, the UEFI firmware and the software TPM this distribution packages
enable and start libvirt, whichever of the monolithic or modular daemons this box has
define, autostart and start libvirt's default NAT network for guests
create the disk, ISO and nvram directories and define the storage pool
add the invoking account to the libvirt group
download the Windows virtio driver ISO and refuse anything that is not an ISO 9660 image
add the IOMMU kernel parameters, after backing up every boot entry and leaving the fallback entries alone
claim one PCI vendor:device pair for vfio-pci so a guest can own it outright — the pair is matched against a four-hex-digit pattern before it is written anywhere
give a claimed PCI device back to its normal driver
start downloading one installer image from the catalog this program carries — an OS id, never an address; Windows images are licensed and are not fetched

adopt an installer image that was fetched as leo into /var/lib/leo/spaces-import — by OS id, after checking it is an ISO — into the root-owned media directory; how a licensed Windows image gets there without a root shell

pack the Leo guest tools leo staged for one space under /var/lib/leo/spaces-import/guest-tools/<space> — the satellite and its installer — into a CD image in the media directory; the space name, never a path or an address
insert accept rules for the guest bridge (DHCP, DNS and forwarding) ahead of the host firewall's drops, and install the unit that re-applies them after any firewall reload
re-insert those rules — what the unit runs at boot; takes nothing
